html:
The Mashco Piro, who call themselves Nomole, are a people of nomadic hunter-gatherers who live in voluntary isolation in the rainforest of southeast Peru, in and around Manú National Park. Their language is Arawakan, close to that of the Yine.

They avoid contact with outsiders, move between camps, and live by hunting, fishing and gathering. It is thought they may be descendants of farmers who fled into the deep forest during the rubber boom, when men like Carlos Fitzcarrald raided the upper Madre de Dios in the 1890s.

Since 2011 groups have appeared more often on river banks, likely pushed by logging and roads. In 2024 they were photographed near logging concessions. Their neighbours include the Matsigenka and the Harakbut in Peru.
